featured_reviews.name: Satyendra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Rating: ★★☆☆☆

I recently moved out after spending five years as a tenant in Sapphire Lakeside, and I want to share my experiences for the benefit of current and future residents.

The society has a lot of potential, with beautiful greenery and open spaces that make it a pleasant place to live. I made some amazing friendships and had wonderful neighbors who made us feel like family.

However, my experience was marred by a significant lack of professionalism from the society manager and staff. The manager’s rude and disrespectful communication set a negative tone, influencing the behavior of the entire staff. Security guards often acted more like enforcers, and the housekeeping staff, including a particularly inappropriate female housekeeping supervisor, were increasingly rude.

While rules and norms are essential, they should be enforced with professionalism and respect. Residents are the primary stakeholders and deserve to be treated with dignity. Proper communication and a respectful attitude are crucial for maintaining a harmonious community.

To improve living conditions, I recommend the following:

•	Embrace modern and sustainable initiatives like separating wet and dry waste and promoting the use of electric vehicles with adequate charging facilities.
•	Invest in hospitality training for staff.
•	Improve fire and safety compliance.

Despite these issues, Sapphire Lakeside holds some of my most cherished memories. I hope the management takes these points into consideration to make Sapphire Lakeside a better place for everyone.

Sincerely,

featured_reviews.name: AQUIB SHAIKH
featured_reviews.review_text:
Powai is a premier, upscale residential and commercial hub in central Mumbai, renowned for its scenic artificial lake built in 1891, the prestigious IIT Bombay, and the Hiranandani township. It combines rapid urban development with green spaces, featuring high-rise, Neo-classical architecture, premium nightlife, and a bustling startup ecosystem.
housing.com
housing.com
+4
Key Highlights of Powai:
Geography & Landmarks: Centered around the 220-hectare Powai Lake (created 1891), the area boasts significant biodiversity, including migratory birds. Key, well-known, and popular landmarks include IIT Bombay, the National Institute of Industrial Engineering (NITIE) (now IIM Mumbai), and the Hiranandani Gardens.
Lifestyle & Culture: Known for its vibrant, cosmopolitan community, the area is packed with trendy cafes, upscale pubs like Madeira & Mime, and restaurants in Hiranandani. The Lakeside Promenade is a popular spot for walking, and Nirvana Park provides greenery.
Economy & Education: Beyond being a residential hotspot, it is a major commercial area hosting corporate parks, IT offices, and startups, earning it the nickname "Startup Valley".
Connectivity: It offers excellent connectivity to the Western Express Highway, Eastern Express Highway, and the JVLR, facilitating travel to Andheri and Ghatkopar railway stations.
Justdial
Justdial
+10
Development & Environment:
The area has transformed from a quiet suburb into a dense, high-end, urban center. The BMC is currently working on initiatives to clean up the Powai Lake, which faces ecological challenges despite being a primary attraction.

featured_reviews.name: LocalGuide Reviews
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’m an owner at L&T Elixir Reserve, and while the project has its positives, the overall experience has been deeply disappointing.

The location is a clear highlight, with a lake and a nearby hillock contributing to a pleasant overall environment. In terms of surroundings and ambience, the project deserves an 8/10.

Unfortunately, execution has fallen far short of expectations from a brand like L&T. The flat delivered has multiple shortcomings, including damaged flooring, damp walls, and poorly finished washroom tiling. These are basic quality issues that should never be present at the time of possession.

The allotted parking spaces are still not ready for use even after possession handover. The lobby level is filled with debris, making it extremely inconvenient and unsafe for residents to move around. Although the clubhouse OC has been received, the clubhouse itself is not even half completed and is clearly unusable.

To make matters worse, during the possession handover, buyers are forced to sign a document stating that they are fully satisfied with the quality and delivery and that they will not raise any concerns afterward. Only after signing this document are the keys handed over. This practice feels coercive, unprofessional, and completely against the trust buyers place in a reputed developer.

Overall, the experience has been so unpleasant that one would rather consider buying from a second-grade builder, as that may actually result in a more transparent and respectful handover process. This is certainly not the standard one expects from L&T.

featured_reviews.name: Rajan Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Disappointed by Stray Dog Menace in L&T

As a resident of L&T Powai, I had high expectations of safety, cleanliness, and responsible management — unfortunately, the growing stray dog menace has been a major letdown.

It’s extremely disturbing and unsafe, especially for children and senior citizens. Packs of dogs roam freely, bark aggressively at pedestrians, chase cyclists, and even enter building premises. Despite multiple complaints, there seems to be no concrete action taken by the township management or the RWA.

Many families are now afraid to let their kids play in open spaces, and early morning or late-night walks have become risky. Instead of addressing the issue, there seems to be more focus on optics than on real safety concerns.

While we all respect animal rights, public safety must come first. If people want to care for stray dogs, they should do it responsibly and not at the cost of others’ safety. We chose to live in a gated community for peace of mind — not to feel like we're navigating danger zones daily.

Requesting L&T authorities to take urgent and effective measures. Ignoring the problem is not a solution.
